messages.author: b2568d0552c4f5e8
messages.subject: matrix-vector product
parts:
If m is a matrix and v1 and v2 are vectors of length matching number of columns in m, I would have thought that the following would work to get exp of inner product of row 1 and vector v1

exp(-(m.row(1)*v1).sum);

but I got compilation errors. Presumably because m.row(1) is not a vector?

Instead I used

v2=m.row(1);
exp(-(v2*v1).sum);

and it worked properly.  Maybe I should have used (m*v1)(1)?  I read through matrix_arrays.cpp but still unclear on some things. Did it fail because m.row(1) is not a vector type and by explicitly setting to a vector it was ok? Thanks for any guidance. Still learning.

regards --jeff

messages.author: 02e03030784aa6a7
messages.subject: Re: matrix-vector product
parts:
I do not have the answer for this, but it usually helps breaking the expression up
into several lines with type explicitly given (as you show).

The difficulty in figuring out what is going on stems from the fact
that "matrix" comes directly from Eigen, while "vector" is implemented in TMB.

I do not think users can be expected to learn all the rules, so
a solution would be to expand matrix_arrays.cpp with a lot more cases.
Maybe a topic for a future TMB workshop?
